slides.heading: Local Variables
slides.body: Local Variables is part of Functions and Modularity. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Local Variables
slides.body: A local variable is created inside a function and mainly belongs to that function. This helps keep different parts of a program separate.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A local variable is like a note kept inside one classroom. It is useful there, but it is not automatically posted everywhere.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: A good function should do one clear task and have a name that explains that task.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a function with a local variable message and print it inside the function.
slides.hint: Assign message inside the function body, then print it.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Define show_total() with local total = 5 and print it.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
